question: Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ be a set satisfying the following properties: (i) if $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ are any two distinct elements in $X$, then either $x_1>x_2$ and $y_1>y_2$, or $x_2>x_1$ and $y_2>y_1$; (ii) there are two elements $(a_1,b_1)$ and $(a_2,b_2)$ in $X$ such that for any $(x,y)$ in $X$, $a_1\le x\le a_2$ and $b_1\le y\le b_2$; (iii) if $(x_1,y_1)$ and $(x_2,y_2)$ are two elements of $X$, then for all $\lambda\in[0,1]$, $(\lambda x_1+(1-\lambda)x_2,\lambda y_1+(1-\lambda)y_2)\in X$. Show that if $(x,y)$ is in $X$, then for some $\lambda\in[0,1]$, $x=\lambda a_1+(1-\lambda)a_2$, $y=\lambda b_1+(1-\lambda)b_2$.

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10 + 2 Level
